key_facts: **Neuropathic (diabetic foot) ulcers** form on insensate pressure points: plantar metatarsal heads, heel and toe tips.
Painless, surrounded by **callus**, with warm feet and good pulses unless neuro-ischaemic.
Test with a **10 g monofilament**; probe to bone and X-ray/MRI for osteomyelitis.
Any diabetic foot ulcer: refer to the multidisciplinary foot service **within 1 working day** (NICE NG19).
Same-day admission for spreading infection, sepsis, crepitus, wet gangrene or suspected Charcot foot.

sections.title: Overview
blocks: A **neuropathic ulcer** follows loss of **protective sensation**, with or without deformity and ischaemia (‘neuro-ischaemic’ foot). Most are **diabetic foot ulcers**, a leading cause of amputation.

sub: Up to a quarter of people with diabetes develop a foot ulcer in their lifetime; most amputations in diabetes follow an ulcer.

sections.title: Aetiology: causes and risk factors
blocks: Peripheral neuropathy (usually diabetes; also alcohol, B12 deficiency, leprosy) means repetitive trauma goes unnoticed. Deep ulcers can reach bone, with a risk of **osteomyelitis**.

ul: **"It doesn't hurt, so it's not serious"**: absence of pain is the problem.

sections.title: Pathophysiology and pathology
blocks: Without **protective sensation**, repeated pressure goes unnoticed and breaks down the skin.

mech.t: Sensory loss removes pain warning; motor neuropathy causes clawing and abnormal pressure; autonomic neuropathy dries and cracks skin.
High plantar pressure builds thick callus, which raises pressure further.
Tissue breaks down beneath the callus and the ulcer deepens towards bone.
mech.caption: Neuropathic plantar ulcer: callus over a deep ulcer above the metatarsal head, with damaged nerve fibres and concentrated pressure.

mech.t: Poor perfusion and impaired immunity let infection spread to bone (osteomyelitis).

histo: Bone biopsy or deep tissue samples guide treatment of osteomyelitis.

ul: Site: **plantar** metatarsal heads, heel, tips of toes, under bunions.
Deep, punched-out, surrounded by **callus**; may reach bone.
Often **painless**; warm foot with good pulses (unless neuro-ischaemic).
Clawed toes, Charcot deformity, dry fissured skin.

sub: Hot, swollen, red foot in neuropathy, often painless: immobilise and refer the same day.

ul: Test sensation with a **10 g monofilament** and vibration.
**Probe to bone**, plus X-ray or MRI if osteomyelitis is suspected.
Deep tissue samples rather than surface swabs if infected.

sections.title: Differential diagnoses
blocks: [Arterial ulcer](condition:arterial-leg-ulcer), pressure ulcer (immobile or paraplegic patients), [venous ulcer](condition:venous-leg-ulcer), malignancy (non-healing).

ul: **Any diabetic foot ulcer:** refer urgently to the **multidisciplinary foot care service** or foot protection service (within 1 working day, NICE NG19).
**Offloading**, glycaemic optimisation, debridement, and assessment for infection, which may need admission and IV antibiotics.
Diabetic foot infection: follow NICE NG19 and local antimicrobial guidance.

ladder.t: Daily foot checks, footwear, podiatry; glycaemic control.
Multidisciplinary foot care service within 1 working day; offloading, debridement.
Antibiotics per NICE NG19 and local guidance; admit if severe.

refer.t: Spreading infection, fever, crepitus, wet necrosis or suspected Charcot foot.

sections.title: Red flags and when to refer

ul: Diabetic foot with **spreading redness, fever, crepitus or wet necrosis**: **ED / same-day admission**.
Probe to bone, or suspected osteomyelitis or **Charcot foot** (hot, swollen foot in neuropathy).
**Never ignore a ‘small’ plantar ulcer in diabetes.**
Many heal with offloading; recurrence is common, so lifelong foot protection is needed.

pearls: Teach **daily foot checks**, sensible footwear and podiatry follow-up; never walk barefoot with neuropathy.
Painless ulcer under a callus suggests neuropathic.
